facial_behavior_observations.observation: In the single detailed ARKit session 20261114-060000-synth01 (duration 44.967 s, 1348 frames, 1303 tracked frames), recorded during prompted markers ['Look left', 'Look right', 'Neutral face', 'Smile'], blink rate was 21.4 per minute (count 16, meanDurationSeconds 0.111, exportedDerivedMeans blink_rate_per_min 20.8), eyeOpenness mean was 0.942, facialMovement variability was 0.041 (amplitude 0.21, activityPerSecond 0.33), headMovement poseVariabilityRad was 0.038 (yaw amplitude 0.375 rad), gaze directionChangeCount was 4, and overallMeanAbsoluteDifference asymmetry was 0.017.
supporting_measurements: headMovement: poseVariabilityRad 0.038, meanAmplitudeRad 0.16, yaw 0.375; asymmetry: overallMeanAbsoluteDifference 0.017, smile 0.06
facial_behavior_observations.data_quality: High face tracking (tracked_fraction 0.9666, quality_score 0.98, missingBlendShapeFraction 0), with cameraStateDistribution limited for 0.044 of frames (insufficientFeatures: 60), 1 faceLostEvents, and 2 estimated dropped frames; windows.60s is empty because the 44.967 s recording is shorter than 60 s.
facial_behavior_observations.limitations: Movements reflect execution of explicit session markers ('Look left', 'Look right', 'Neutral face', 'Smile'), so blend-shape activations such as mouthSmile_L (mean 0.112, maximum 0.68) and head yaw represent task-directed physical motion rather than spontaneous facial behavior or any emotional state.

facial_behavior_observations.observation: Across the 5 daily rows from 2026-11-10 to 2026-11-14 (1 facial window per day), blinkRatePerMinute ranged from 18.7 (2026-11-13) to 24.1 (2026-11-11), facialVariability ranged from 0.031 (2026-11-11) to 0.043 (2026-11-13), headPoseVariabilityRad ranged from 0.029 (2026-11-11) to 0.04 (2026-11-13), and eyeOpennessMean ranged from 0.931 (2026-11-11) to 0.947 (2026-11-13).
facial_behavior_observations.data_quality: Only 5 daily rows and 1 full ARKit session object are provided in detail, whereas baseline_profile.facialReferences reports 9 daysCovered; trackedFraction varied from 0.91 on 2026-11-11 to 0.99 on 2026-11-13.
facial_behavior_observations.limitations: Each day's facial summary rests on facialWindowCount 1 (a single brief morning session around 06:00 to 06:15 in session IDs), which cannot capture daytime variability in facial, eye, or head movement.

cross_modal_patterns.observation: HRV and facial movement variability showed a positive descriptive association over 9 paired days at lag 0 (pearsonR 0.62, spearmanRho 0.58), but day-to-day values in the 5 visible daily rows were not strictly monotonic: for example, on 2026-11-14 HRV was 41.7 ms with facialVariability 0.041, whereas 2026-11-10 and 2026-11-12 had higher HRV (46.2 and 44.6 ms) with lower facialVariability (0.039 and 0.04).
supporting_measurements: correlations: HeartRateVariabilitySDNN vs facialVariability, lagDays 0, pairedPoints 9, pearsonR 0.62, spearmanRho 0.58
daily_rows non-monotonic points: 2026-11-10 (HRV 46.2, facialVariability 0.039), 2026-11-12 (HRV 44.6, facialVariability 0.04), 2026-11-14 (HRV 41.7, facialVariability 0.041)
cross_modal_patterns.data_quality: Computed on 9 paired days (4 paired days are not shown in daily_rows); daily HRV is averaged from sparse readings (2 to 4 samples/day in listed days) and facialVariability comes from 1 short session per day.
cross_modal_patterns.limitations: Descriptive correlation with n = 9 and no significance or multiple-comparison testing; could be confounded by how vigorously prompted tasks ('Smile', 'Look left', 'Look right') were performed, face tracking fraction (0.91 on 2026-11-11 vs 0.99 on 2026-11-13), lighting, or HRV measurement timing.

cross_modal_patterns.observation: No correlation entry is provided between SleepAnalysis (wake-up day) and general facial or head movement variability; across the 5 visible daily rows, the shortest sleep day (2026-11-11: 6.2) coincided with the lowest facialVariability (0.031) and headPoseVariabilityRad (0.029) and the longest sleep day (2026-11-13: 8.1) coincided with the highest facialVariability (0.043) and headPoseVariabilityRad (0.04), whereas 2026-11-10 had more sleep (7.8) than 2026-11-12 (7.4) and 2026-11-14 (7.5) but lower facialVariability (0.039 vs 0.04 and 0.041) and headPoseVariabilityRad (0.036 vs 0.037 and 0.038).
cross_modal_patterns.data_quality: Correlation coefficients for SleepAnalysis vs facialVariability or headPoseVariabilityRad are omitted from correlations, and 4 of the 9 recording days are absent from daily_rows.
cross_modal_patterns.limitations: With only 5 visible paired days, missing correlation coefficients, 2-source sleep aggregation, and task-prompted recording sessions, a consistent relationship between wake-day sleep duration and overall facial movement cannot be established.

cross_modal_patterns.limitations: Small sample (9 paired days) where extreme days (such as 2026-11-11, which also had lower trackedFraction 0.91) can heavily influence Pearson and Spearman coefficients; potential confounders include illness, medication, hydration, phone positioning, and task prompt execution.

cross_modal_patterns.observation: Activity metrics showed weak or uncomputed associations with facial and head movement: StepCount vs next-day headPoseVariabilityRad (lagDays 1) had near-zero correlation over 8 paired days (pearsonR 0.12, spearmanRho 0.1), AppleExerciseTime vs facialVariability at lagDays 0 was not computed because it had only 5 paired days (fewer than 7), same-day (lag 0) step correlations are not listed, and active/basal energy measurements are entirely absent.

correlations: AppleExerciseTime vs facialVariability, lagDays 0, pairedPoints 5, pearsonR null, spearmanRho null
cross_modal_patterns.data_quality: StepCount merges 2 overlapping sources using the daily maximum; AppleExerciseTime has no daily values or summary statistics in the input; energy expenditure metrics are completely missing; morning ARKit sessions around 06:00 UTC occur before most same-day step accumulation.
cross_modal_patterns.limitations: Morning facial recordings precede the rest of that day's physical activity (making lag-0 activity associations temporally ambiguous), while lag-1 steps showed practically no linear or rank association over 8 paired days.

cross_modal_patterns.observation: SleepAnalysis and blinkRatePerMinute at lag 0 had the largest-magnitude correlation among reported pairs over 9 paired days (pearsonR -0.71, spearmanRho -0.67); across all 5 visible daily rows, shorter wake-day sleep aligned with higher blinkRatePerMinute and slightly lower eyeOpennessMean (ranging from SleepAnalysis 6.2 with blinkRatePerMinute 24.1 and eyeOpennessMean 0.931 on 2026-11-11 to SleepAnalysis 8.1 with blinkRatePerMinute 18.7 and eyeOpennessMean 0.947 on 2026-11-13).

cross_modal_patterns.data_quality: Based on 9 paired days (4 days omitted from daily_rows); other blink statistics (such as meanDurationSeconds 0.111 and meanInterBlinkIntervalSeconds 2.79) are only present for the single 2026-11-14 session, so their relationship with sleep cannot be checked.
cross_modal_patterns.limitations: Purely descriptive over 9 brief (~45 s) windows without multiple-comparison adjustment across 56 candidate pairs; plausible confounders include tracking quality (0.91 on 2026-11-11 vs 0.99 on 2026-11-13), ambient light, ocular surface dryness, contact lens or screen use, time elapsed since waking, and 2-source sleep selection.

cross_modal_patterns.observation: Self-reported wellbeing, mood, or symptom ratings are completely absent from the input data, so no relationship between self-reported wellbeing and physiological or facial measurements can be examined.
supporting_measurements: health.metrics (only HeartRateVariabilitySDNN present; no wellbeing entries in daily_rows, correlations, or baseline_profile)

cross_modal_patterns.limitations: Without timestamped self-report questionnaires, subjective state cannot be compared against HealthKit or ARKit variables.

longitudinal_changes.limitations: Sparse daily sampling (~3.25 readings/day) and the 79200 s gap during the week of 2026-10-26 could contribute to the lower weekly mean of 36.4 ms without necessarily reflecting a sustained physiological shift.

longitudinal_changes.limitations: Five days of paired rows are too short to distinguish multi-week longitudinal change from ordinary day-to-day fluctuation.

potential_confounders.observation: Execution of prompted recording markers ('Look left', 'Look right', 'Neutral face', 'Smile'), small paired-day counts (5 to 9 days across 56 screened pairs without multiple-comparison correction), multi-source device selection for sleep and steps, sparse HRV sampling, and unrecorded factors (medication, illness, caffeine, ocular dryness, or time since waking) may drive or obscure the observed correlations.

potential_confounders.limitations: With 56 health-by-facial pairs screened on n = 8 to 9 days, moderate-to-large correlation magnitudes (such as -0.71 or 0.62) can arise by chance or from a single atypical day.

recommended_tracking: Collect daily ARKit recordings across at least 21 to 30+ days at a standardized post-wake interval, separating unprompted neutral-gaze segments from prompted movement tasks ('Look left', 'Look right', 'Smile') and logging ambient light, phone distance (meanDistanceToOriginM), and camera tracking quality for every session.

Export complete daily series and summary statistics (including units, device source IDs, and timestamps) for SleepAnalysis, RestingHeartRate, StepCount, AppleExerciseTime, and active/basal energy expenditure so morning recordings can be aligned strictly with prior-day vs post-recording activity.
Include session-level blink duration, inter-blink interval, and recorder-derived blink rates across all days to cross-check hysteresis blink counts (e.g., 21.4 vs 20.8 per min on 2026-11-14).

Add brief, timestamped daily self-report logs for perceived wellbeing plus contextual confounders (caffeine, medication, illness, contact lens or screen use, and eye dryness) if wellbeing associations are to be studied.
parsed.plain_language_explanation: Over the 31-day period from October 15 to November 14, 2026, Apple Health recorded heart rate variability (HRV) on 30 days (median 44.6 ms across 95 sparse readings, averaging 3.25 per day) alongside 9 days of brief morning face-tracking recordings (~45 seconds on November 14, using prompted movements: 'Look left', 'Look right', 'Neutral face', 'Smile'). Across the 9 paired days, higher daily HRV had a moderate positive descriptive association with facial movement variability (Pearson r = 0.62, Spearman rho = 0.58), higher resting heart rate had a moderate negative association with facial movement variability (r = -0.49, rho = -0.45), and longer wake-day sleep duration had a negative association with blink rate (r = -0.71, rho = -0.67). However, in the 5 days of detailed daily rows (November 10–14), day-to-day values for HRV and resting heart rate were not strictly ordered with facial variability, previous-day step counts showed virtually no association with head pose variability (r = 0.12 over 8 days), exercise minutes had too few paired days (5) to compute a correlation, and neither energy expenditure nor self-reported wellbeing was present in the data. HRV median was nearly unchanged from the first week (45.3 ms) to the last week (44.6 ms), despite a lower weekly average during the week of October 26 (36.4 ms), while multi-week trends for facial movement and other health metrics could not be assessed from the 5 detailed days. All observed associations describe physical movement and physiological readings in a very small sample without implying causation, emotion, or clinical conditions, and they could easily reflect differences in face-tracking quality (0.91 to 0.99), lighting, how prompted facial tasks were performed, or sparse watch sampling.
